title: Flash Evaporator
model_title: Flash Evaporator (Heater → Pressure Reduction → Flash Vessel)

introduction.definition: A flash evaporator separates vapour from a liquid by a sudden drop in pressure. The liquid is first heated under pressure so it cannot boil; it then passes a pressure-reducing valve into a vessel at lower pressure, where part of it flashes into vapour. The vapour leaves through a demister at the top and the concentrated liquid from the bottom.
applications: Concentration of solutions without heating surfaces in the vessel
key_points: No heating surface in the flash vessel — less fouling
Vessel pressure sets the flashing temperature
introduction.summary: A flash evaporator separates vapour from a liquid by sudden pressure reduction. The liquid is heated under pressure, then throttled into a vessel at lower pressure; part of it instantly boils ("flashes"), cooling the rest. Vapour leaves through a demister at the top, the concentrated liquid from the bottom.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Fraction flashed rises with the difference between inlet temperature and vessel saturation temperature.

pressure.title: Pressure drop causes flashing
pressure.description: The feed is heated under pressure so it does not boil. Passing the pressure-reducing valve into the lower-pressure vessel, it is suddenly above its boiling point at the new pressure: part of it flashes to vapour, and the latent heat taken by that vapour cools the remaining liquid to the saturation temperature of the vessel. Flash fraction ≈ cp·(T_in − T_sat) / h_fg.

foundation: Support vessels on structure/legs designed for operating and flooded weights; allow thermal growth of calandrias and vapour lines.
alignment: Vertical calandrias plumb (falling-film distribution depends on it); slope liquor lines for drainage.
piping: Vapour lines sized for low ΔP; condensate drained by traps or level control; vents for non-condensables on each steam chest.
Vacuum system (condenser + vacuum pump/ejector) for the last effect.
commissioning: Leak/vacuum test; water trials (wetting, levels); bring steam on slowly; set levels and densities; CIP routine.

routine.task: Monitor vessel pressure, level and vapour quality.

periodic.task: Check demister ΔP; inspect flash valve trim.

overhaul.task: Inspect vessel for erosion at the inlet.

lubrication: No lubrication for the static parts — lubricate valve stems, rotating parts and drives per maker.

safety: Relief valve on vessel; flashing hot liquid and steam burn hazard.

script.narration: This module introduces the Flash Evaporator.
A flash evaporator separates vapour from a liquid by a sudden drop in pressure.
The liquid is first heated under pressure so it cannot boil; it then passes a pressure-reducing valve into a vessel at lower pressure, where part of it flashes into vapour.
The vapour leaves through a demister at the top and the concentrated liquid from the bottom.
Typical applications include multi-stage flash (MSF) desalination stages; condensate and blowdown flash recovery; concentration of solutions without heating surfaces in the vessel.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

video_tutorials.title: Flash Evaporator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Flash Evaporator.
Monitor vessel pressure, level and vapour quality.
Check demister ΔP; inspect flash valve trim.
Inspect vessel for erosion at the inlet.
Watch for carry-over of liquid: contaminated vapour/condensate. Common cause: demister damaged, high level, foaming.
Watch for valve erosion: poor control. Common cause: two-phase flashing flow.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
